 Follow Houston weather: Rain likely on Sunday. When will the heaviest rainfall occur?
 Mary Wasson Sun, November 8, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A large storm system will move into Texas on Sunday with widespread rain and storms across the southern half of the state. (Weather Prediction Center) Expect soggy and dreary weather Sunday across Southeast Texas, as scattered rain slowly moves in. It will accompany the most recent atmospheric disturbance moving across the southern half of the Lone Star State, from the Big Bend area into South Texas.
 While the bulk of the rain will generally fall west and south of Houston, the region still has a solid 30% to 50% chance of rain in the afternoon, especially west of Interstate 45.
 Timing of the rain
 We'll wake up to overcast skies with a few light showers or sprinkles across the region. Winds will be out of the northeast at 5 to 10 mph, with temperatures in the low 60s.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Scattered showers may drift a little farther east throughout the day, with rain chances increasing during the late afternoon and evening. High temperatures will climb to near 70 degrees.
 This map of Southeast Texas shows what weather radar could look like at 9 a.m. Sunday, based on the rain forecast from the GFS forecast model. (Pivotal)
 By Sunday evening, we could see a lull in activity before another round of rain moves in, and linger through early next week.
 Forecast for next week
 Cloudy skies will stick around through the first half of next week, along with low rain chances through Wednesday, especially during the afternoon.
 Rain chances will stick around through midweek before drying out and warming up later in the week. (National Weather Service)
 As far as temperatures go, it will feel rather comfortable, with morning lows ranging from 58 to 63 degrees and afternoon highs reaching the upper 60s to lower 70s through Wednesday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Sunshine will make a return by Thursday, with temperatures settling back into early-November averages of 54 degrees in the morning and 76 degrees in the afternoon.
 Rainfall totals
 The heaviest rainfall will be concentrated across Central and South Texas, west of a line from College Station to Columbus to Bay City, and those areas will have a higher probability of receiving at least a half-inch of rain, according to the National Weather Service.
 Rainfall totals will be higher west of Houston from Sunday through Tuesday. (National Weather Service)
 So far this month, Houston has picked up just under an inch of rain, putting the city ahead of its normal pace for November. However, the city has recorded 37.7 inches of rainfall so far this year, still about 7 inches below its normal year-to-date total. Any new rainfall will be welcome, and the latest outlooks suggest wet weather could remain in the forecast through the rest of the month.
